exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS/Passive DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Unclassified zone data can be harvested through passive DNS reconnaissance, exposing sensitive internal DNS records to adversaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of sensitivity classification on zone data facilitates adversary gathering of DNS information about victim infrastructure.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: IP Addresses
exploitedBy.relevance: Indefinitely retained DNS records expose historical IP address mappings that adversaries can use to map victim network infrastructure.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: NTDS
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted zone file snapshots at rest are analogous to credential store dumps, allowing attackers who gain storage access to extract sensitive DNS data in plaintext.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Valid Accounts
exploitedBy.relevance: Overly broad read access means any compromised valid account can access full zone data, amplifying the impact of credential compromise.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Windows File and Directory Permissions Modification
exploitedBy.relevance: Misconfigured or excessively permissive access controls on zone data reflect improper permission management that adversaries can exploit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: File Deletion
exploitedBy.relevance: Without a formal disposal procedure, DNS record data is not properly sanitized or deleted, leaving residual data accessible to adversaries who can recover it.
